# User Research Methods

[conditional] Read when the owner can reach real end users for this
topic. The default flow has one interlocutor and never blocks on
research; when users are reachable these methods add evidence, and their
findings still enter the brief only through BR/AC entries, the
assumption ledger and open questions, never around them.

## Ground Rules

- Research answers a named question from the brief (an open question, an
  assumption row, a contested grouping); DON'T run a method to "learn
  things".
- A finding without a session citation (who, when, what was observed)
  does not enter the ledger.
- User preferences are laddered like owner preferences: the why behind
  them is the requirement; the vote count is not.
- A handful of users per round surfaces most blocking issues; a second
  small round beats one large round.

## Structured Interviews at Scale

The same script across several users so answers are comparable; build
the script from the brief's open questions and assumption rows.

- Output artifact: a finding list. Each finding cites its sessions and
  proposes a disposition: confirm an assumption row, mint a BR or AC, or
  open a question.
- DON'T average contradictory answers into one rule; a contradiction
  between users is itself a finding, routed to the owner as a decision.

## Card Sorting

Users group and label the domain's items in their own words; exposes the
vocabulary and groupings the conceptual data dictionary must speak.

- Output artifact: a grouping table with an agreement level per item.
  High-agreement labels feed dictionary naming; contested items become
  open questions.
- Signal to run it: the owner and the users are suspected to use
  different words for the same records, or the dictionary's entity names
  keep getting corrected mid-conversation.

## Tree Testing

Users locate items in a proposed hierarchy from task prompts, before any
screens exist; tests whether the brief's structure matches how users
think.

- Output artifact: a task success table (task, success rate, wrong paths
  taken). A failed navigation-critical task becomes an AC on the
  affected flow or an open question against the structure.
- Keep the altitude: the finding is "users cannot find X under Y"; the
  fix (renaming, restructuring, navigation) belongs to the design chain.

## Usability Observation

Watch one user at a time attempt real tasks against the demo or the
mockups; say nothing, log everything.

- Output artifact: an observation log per session: task, where the user
  hesitated, where they failed, what they said. Each blocking
  observation becomes a proposed BR/AC change or an open question;
  purely visual friction routes to the design chain unchanged.
- Boundary: this method tests whether the brief's flows survive contact
  with users; critiquing visual design is the designer's evaluation, not
  this one.
